html:
The great gilded stupa on a hill in Yangon, the most sacred Buddhist site in Myanmar. It rises about 99 metres and can be seen across the city.

Tradition says it holds eight hairs of the Buddha and is 2,600 years old. Historians think the Mon built the first stupa here between the 500s and 900s. Later rulers made it larger:

  • in 1362 King Binnya U of Pegu raised it to 18 metres;
  • Queen Shin Sawbu, in the 1400s, raised it to 40 metres and gave her own weight in gold to cover it;
  • in 1774, after an earthquake, King Hsinbyushin of the Konbaung dynasty rebuilt it to its present height.

The spire is covered in gold plates and its crown is set with thousands of diamonds and rubies. It has also been a place of protest: students struck here against British rule in 1920, and in 1988 Aung San Suu Kyi spoke to a crowd of hundreds of thousands at its foot.
sum: The great gilded stupa on a hill in Yangon, the most sacred Buddhist site in Myanmar. It rises about 99 metres and can be seen across the city.
